packageRules.description: vikunja: the image is tracked by the custom regex manager (the mirror registry+tag pattern) and the charts by the vendir manager (git ref / helmChart version in vendir.yml). Disable the auto helm managers on the Application valuesObject and the vendored charts — helm-values otherwise concatenates the image registry+repository into a malformed dep, and helm-values/helmv3 would raise spurious PRs editing vendir-managed Chart.yaml/values.yaml. vendored/bjw-s-common is the common subchart vendored as its own sibling directory (see vendir.yml) — without it here, helm-values scans its default values.yaml directly and opens PRs bumping unused addon image tags (gluetun, code-server, ...) that vendir just overwrites on the next sync.
CNPG operator — vendored whole-release via vendir (not per-image)
Barman Cloud Plugin — vendored whole-release via vendir
cert-manager — vendored whole-release via vendir (replaces per-image grouping)
external-secrets CRDs — vendored via vendir. NOTE: this git ref must track the Helm chart version in application.external-secrets.yaml; bumps are independent and can drift — review together.

vikunja's bjw-s common subchart — vendored via vendir's helmChart fetch into vendored/bjw-s-common/base (a plain symlink at vendored/vikunja/base/charts/common points there; see vendir.yml). Pinned at 1.5.1: go-vikunja/helm-chart (latest tag v2.0.2) still assumes bjw-s-common's pre-2.0 single `controller:` schema, while common >=2.0 replaced it with a `controllers:` map — `helm template` against 5.0.1 fails outright with "No enabled controller found with identifier 'main'". Re-enable once go-vikunja/helm-chart ships a release compatible with the newer common schema.
Contour — vendored whole-release via vendir; envoy image is tracked separately via kubernetes manager on the overlay patch
metrics-server — vendored whole-release via vendir (not per-image)
kubelet-rubber-stamp — group vendir ref and image tag bumps together
thanos is handled by the custom regex manager with a registryUrl annotation (registryAliases maps to DockerHub but thanos lives on quay.io)
cloudflared is mirrored from cloudflare/cloudflared on DockerHub
mongodb_exporter publishes 0.x releases; require review before a major-line change
Bump altinity-clickhouse-operator chart and CRD git ref together
Group ClickHouse server and keeper images together
Group exportarr sidecars into a single PR
Group VPA components into a single PR

democratic-csi sidecars and snapshot-controller — csi-snapshotter and snapshot-controller must stay on the same version, and the sidecar set is validated together upstream (k8s e2e bumps them in lockstep)
Only update kube-prometheus-stack on Fridays
Only update Sonarr on Fridays
Only update SABnzbd on Fridays
Only update Radarr on Fridays
Only update Prowlarr on Fridays
thanos-receive-controller uses date-based tags (main-YYYY-MM-DD-hash)
selfoss uses monotonic date-based tags (YYYYMMDD-githash); docker versioning treats the hash as a compatibility suffix and filters out every other tag, so parse the date as a single integer instead

searxng uses date-based tags (YYYY.M.D-githash); same compatibility-suffix trap as selfoss — parse the date components and ignore the hash. Wildcard because the mirror-registry depName keeps its registry.apps.nickv.me prefix (registryAliases only rewrites packageName).

cloudnative-vectorchord tags are PGMAJOR-VCMAJOR.VCMINOR.VCPATCH (e.g. 17-0.4.3); docker versioning treats the VectorChord semver as a compatibility suffix and filters out every other tag, so map all four numeric components (regex versioning parses the build group as a 4th release component). Immich accepts VectorChord >=0.3,<2.0. VectorChord-major bumps (17-1.x) roll the cluster, then need ALTER EXTENSION vchord UPDATE; REINDEX INDEX face_index; REINDEX INDEX clip_index; (per Immich docs). PG-major bumps (18-x) are offline in-place pg_upgrades, not rolling restarts: CNPG stops every pod, runs pg_upgrade --link on the primary PVC, then re-clones the replicas — source and target images must share a distro (upstream builds every tag on -system-bookworm), the barman plugin serverName must change in the same PR (the plugin never splits archives across majors, and the post-upgrade timeline-1 WAL would overwrite the old archive), and the cluster needs a fresh base backup and ANALYZE right after. Never automerge VC-major or PG-major bumps.

hyperdx MongoDBCommunity spec.version — the community-operator combines spec.version with its own '-ubi8' suffix to build the mongod image tag, so the file must carry the bare semver; extractVersion rewrites releases like 8.0.29-ubi8 to 8.0.29 before comparison/replacement (non-ubi8 tags are dropped). Pinned to exactly 8.0.4, not the 8.0.x stream: mongod 8.0.29 refuses to start on Linux kernel >=6.19 (SERVER-121912 fatal version gate; the cluster workers run 7.0.0 — observed crashing hyperdx-1 after PR #420), while 8.0.4 starts fine with the MONGODB_CONFIG_OVERRIDE_NOTCMALLOC bypass in hyperdx-mongo.yaml. Where the gate first appears in the 8.0.x stream is unverified. Re-pin to a newer stream only after a release confirmed to start on this kernel.
renovate-release-api: self-built; latest = newest CI build of the default branch, tracked by digest (docs/renovate-private-registry-datasource-design.md)
cukk: self-built; latest = newest CI build of the default branch, tracked by digest (docs/renovate-private-registry-datasource-design.md)
python-envoy-authz: self-built; latest = newest CI build of the default branch, tracked by digest
cpu-benchmark: self-built, rebuilt by hand rarely; latest is the only tag, tracked by digest

democratic-csi driver: self-built fork; latest = newest CI build, tracked by digest — hex commit tags ride along as releases but never order. The latest tag was bootstrapped by copying 146445b; the CI push list must keep publishing latest.

jellyfin: self-built fork tags vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH-suffix. The ^v anchor filters the unprefixed junk tags; the suffix must NOT be a (?<compatibility>) capture — that splits tag lines and suppresses updates (the selfoss trap; docs/renovate-private-registry-datasource-design.md)
homelab-pki: self-built semver tags; tftest never passes the service's tag filter

jellyfin.yaml and python-envoy-authz.yaml are also scanned by the kubernetes manager, where registryAliases maps the mirror host to Docker Hub — these self-built repos don't exist there. The regex-manager annotation (custom datasource) owns them; disable the broken duplicate dep (thanos pattern).
